stemMd: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Belmont found that a fog-collecting net works better when its mesh is coarse enough to let air through than when the mesh is as fine as possible.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Belmont gave up on mesh nets once she discovered that fog is pushed around them rather than through them.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Fog rolls inland over Cerro Alto on most mornings, even though the town receives almost no rain.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The main obstacle to collecting fog water at Cerro Alto is that foggy mornings there are rare.

explanationMd:
The main idea is the point the whole passage is built to make, so it has to cover the passage's turn: the expectation Belmont started from, and the result that overturned it.

The passage moves in three steps. It describes the nets, reports that Belmont chose a very fine weave because she expected a denser mesh to intercept more droplets, and then reports that the fine nets did worst while a coarser mesh yielded nearly three times as much water. The option about a coarser mesh outperforming the finest possible weave is the only one that carries that reversal.

A quick way to check a main-idea answer is to ask whether the passage would still need its last three sentences if the option were true. The option about fog arriving on most mornings is a true detail from the first sentence, but the passage does not exist to tell you about the weather; everything after sentence one would be surplus. The options about abandoning the nets and about fog being rare are not supported at all.

distractorRationale.b: The passage never says Belmont gave up on nets. Air being pushed around the fine weave is the reason the fine nets failed, and her response was a coarser mesh, not abandonment of the method.
distractorRationale.d: This contradicts the first sentence, which says thick fog rolls inland on most mornings. The scarcity at Cerro Alto is rain, not fog, which is exactly why fog collection is worth trying there.
distractorRationale.c: This is an accurate detail, but it is the passage's setting rather than its point. A main idea has to account for the experiment and its surprising result, and this sentence says nothing about either.

accessibilityText: Using the passage about Nadia Belmont's fog-collecting mesh nets at Cerro Alto, choose the statement that best expresses the passage's main idea.

provenance.notes: Original item. One distractor is a true detail from the passage, so the item turns on the difference between a supporting fact and the central claim.

review.author: digital-sat-wave4-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The passage builds to the finding that the fine weave performed worst because air could not pass, while a coarser mesh yielded nearly three times as much water. B contradicts the text (she switched to coarser mesh, not away from nets); C is background detail only; D contradicts 'fog rolls inland on most mornings'.

review.notes: Author's own solve and uniqueness check: C is the only option covering the passage's reversal (fine mesh expected to be best, coarse mesh actually best). D is true but is setting, not the point; A and B contradict the text, so no second option is defensible. Not published: awaiting a blind independent solve by a second party. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
